open_obligations: Check whether the two papers mean the same thing by 'process supervision'.
Check Lightman et al.'s confounders: the PRM data was actively selected and smaller.
Note that Lightman et al. do not train the generator with RL, so competitiveness under RL is untested.
out.other_title: Without infrastructure, outcome-based training may outcompete process supervision
out.rationale: Reppert et al. expect that, without scalable infrastructure to support it, outcome-based training will eventually outcompete process supervision performance-wise. Lightman et al. state that their results show process supervision incurs a negative alignment tax.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether process-based supervision must lose to outcome-based training on performance, for reward models on MATH

text: The authors argue that in some cases safer methods for AI systems can carry an alignment tax (reduced performance) and that any alignment tax may hinder adoption, and state that their results show process supervision incurs a negative alignment tax, which could lead to increased adoption of process supervision that they believe would have positive alignment side-effects.
title: Process supervision has a negative alignment tax on math
